idiom_name: fmt::formatter specialization + free-function helpers called by the renderer
implementation_notes: The J2EE helper class is replaced by two ordinary C++ constructs: a fmt::formatter<T> specialization (or a format_as overload) that teaches the formatting library how to present a domain value, and an ordinary free function that the renderer or template engine calls for a fragment. {fmt} requires only a minimal C++11 subset, so this works on pre-C++20 toolchains, and the same formatter is reused by log lines, exceptions and console output for free. Keep a helper class only where the helper genuinely owns configuration - a locale, a currency table, tenant rules - and pass that instance into the render context instead of hiding it in a static.
pitfalls: The specialization must be visible before its point of instantiation; one hidden in a .cpp file silently degrades to a non-formattable-type error at the call site.
A helper that returns complete markup takes over escaping from the template layer; format values, not whole HTML fragments, whenever the engine can still escape them.
The {fmt} dependency is a build-system decision: pin a version and keep the single-header form available for small services and for toolchains without a package manager.

variants.name: std::formatter specialization with std::format (C++20)
variants.implementation_notes: With a C++20 toolchain the same helper needs no third-party dependency: specialize std::formatter<T> in <format> and format fragments with std::format. The specialization is the parse/format pair required by the formatting library, so it composes with the standard format specification, and the helper stays a free function. Prefer this variant on greenfield C++20 projects; keep the {fmt} variant where the toolchain is older, where the library's richer formatters (ranges, chrono, compile-time format strings) are wanted, or where the same formatter must also serve C++11 builds.
pitfalls: std::format may be missing from older standard libraries even when the compiler advertises C++20; feature-test with __cpp_lib_format instead of by standard version.
parse() must return an iterator to the closing brace of the replacement field; returning begin() unconditionally is only correct while the specialization supports no format specifier.
